blocks.text: Organize your Slack workspace for better project flow

A project coordinator needs a clean workspace. Start by naming your channels consistently. Use prefixes like proj- for active projects, team- for internal groups, and client- for external communication. This keeps your list sorted and predictable.

Do not let your channel list grow wild. Archive old projects once they reach completion. Use the sidebar settings to group your channels into sections. You can drag and drop channels into these sections to keep your most urgent project updates at the top of your view.
Essential Slack keyboard shortcuts for Mac

Speed is vital when you are juggling multiple project updates. Memorizing a few key shortcuts will save you hours of menu navigation. Press Command + / to see the full list of shortcuts inside the app.

items: Command + K: Open the quick switcher to jump to any conversation.
Command + F: Search messages in the current channel.
Command + G: Perform a general search across all workspaces.
Shift + Enter: Add a new line to your message without sending it.
Command + ,: Open your Slack preferences to manage notification settings.

blocks.text: Constant pings are the enemy of deep work. As a project coordinator, you need to know when a blocker arises, but you do not need every status update in real time. Open your Slack preferences by pressing Command + , and navigate to the Notifications tab.

Set your notification schedule to match your working hours. Use the Do Not Disturb feature by typing /dnd in any channel to pause alerts when you are in a meeting or drafting a project report. You can also mute specific noisy channels by right clicking the channel name in the sidebar and selecting Mute channel.
Use threads to keep project history clear

Avoid cluttering the main channel feed with long conversations. If a topic requires more than three replies, move it to a thread. This keeps the main feed clean for high level project updates. To reply in a thread, hover over the message and click the speech bubble icon.

Threads also make searching for decisions easier later. When you search for a keyword, Slack includes results from threads. This is a common pain point for coordinators who lose track of where a decision was made.

Slack can occasionally slow down on macOS, especially if you are in many workspaces. If the app feels sluggish, clear your cache. Go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This often resolves performance issues without losing your message history.

If you are missing notifications, check your macOS system settings. Go to System Settings > Notifications > Slack and ensure that banners and sounds are enabled. Sometimes a simple app update fixes these issues.

faq.question: How do I jump to a specific project channel quickly?
faq.answer: Use Command + K to open the quick switcher, then type the first few letters of the channel name.

faq.question: Can I search for files across all my Slack channels?
faq.answer: Yes, press Command + G to open the general search bar. You can use modifiers like has:file to narrow down your search results.

faq.question: How do I stop Slack from sending notifications during meetings?
faq.answer: Type /dnd followed by the duration, such as /dnd 1 hour, to pause notifications immediately.
